title: Permissive CORS on Local Daemon Enables Browser-Based Workstation Takeover
description: The daemon binds to 127.0.0.1:8765 and returns Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * on all endpoints. Malicious websites can execute cross-origin requests to shutdown the PC, exfiltrate memories, or poison decisions.
remediation: Remove Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * and enforce Host header validation or local token authorization.

title: Default-Allow Logic When Allowed Numbers List is Empty Leaves Daemon Unprotected
description: If allowed_numbers is empty, incoming remote messages skip the authentication gate, allowing any Telegram user to execute arbitrary commands before pairing.
remediation: Enforce default-deny pairing: require /auth PIN whenever allowed_numbers is empty or sender is unrecognized.

title: Partial PIN Exposure in Remote Rejection Message Enables Rapid Brute-Force
description: Unauthenticated access rejections leak the first two digits of the secret PIN, reducing search complexity from 10,000 to 100 attempts.
remediation: Omit PIN digits in rejection messages and implement rate limiting.

title: Indirect Prompt Injection via Untrusted Workspace Git Metadata in LLM System Prompt
description: Active workspace context ingests commit messages, branch names, and PR titles directly into the system prompt without boundary encapsulation.
remediation: Wrap external metadata inside <untrusted_workspace_metadata> tags with instructions to ignore embedded directives.

title: Unsanitized Subcommand Concatenation in Remote /git Command Dispatch
description: The /git command uses string interpolation into shell=True, enabling accidental or intentional shell operator chaining.
remediation: Tokenize git arguments and execute with shell=False.
